title: Kairos Power gets up to $100M from Samsung group to build nuclear reactor for Google
slides: Can Kairos Power's nuclear reactor power Google?
It just got $100M from Samsung group
The reactor uses molten salt cooling, not water
This enables factory-built modular reactors for data centers
One action: watch for first deployment by 2030
thread_text:
1. Google's Nuclear Bet

Kairos Power just secured $100M from Samsung Group to build molten-salt cooled nuclear reactors — the first real test of whether Big Tech's energy crisis can be solved by advanced nuclear.

2. Samsung's $100M Signal

The investment isn't just capital — it's a validation from a major industrial player that factory-built reactors can scale. Google's power needs are growing faster than renewables can cover.

3. Water-Free Cooling

Molten salt cooling replaces the need for massive water supplies, enabling reactors to be built almost anywhere — including near data centers. That changes the geography of energy.

4. Modular by Design

These reactors are small enough to be factory-assembled and shipped to site. That means faster, cheaper deployment — exactly what AI data centers need as demand surges.

5. 2030 Deadline

One action: mark 2030 in your calendar. If Kairos hits its first deployment target, it will be the moment nuclear becomes a real option for tech. Watch this space.

Google’s data centers could soon run on nuclear reactors cooled by molten salt instead of water. ⚡

Kairos Power just got up to $100M from Samsung Group to build them.

They’re factory-built and modular, so deployment is faster and cheaper. First target: 2030.

If you publish or create with AI, the energy crunch behind your tools just got a new possible fix. 🔋
